A streamer paid me $8,000 for a GTA 6 server website I built in under 5 minutes.

He wanted a hub for his upcoming GTA 6 online server. Roleplay jobs. Application forms. Server rules. An FAQ. A Discord link. The kind of build an agency charges $8,000 for and ships in 3 weeks.

I opened Claude.

One prompt. I described the server, the jobs, the apply button, the whole layout. Hit send. Waited 2 minutes.

Out came the full site copy. Every page. Every section. Ready to paste.

Then I found an AI website builder. Dropped the prompt in. Pressed one white arrow.

The site loaded. Jobs, rules, FAQ, apply-now button, all live.

I hopped on a call and published it while he watched.

$8,000.

I didn’t write a line of code. I didn’t design a single page. I copied one prompt and pressed one button.

5 minutes. One prompt. $8,000. Next I’m doing it to every streamer alive.

Why did everyone stop learning during the World Cup—except Belgium?
Study time dropped 30% on average across 23 countries during match windows. Morocco and Ghana hit -73%. Argentina -58%. Brazil -56%.

Belgium? Up 53%. Their DataCamp learners skew heavily academic—university students finishing coursework on a deadline. They don't stop for the game.

People are treating AI literacy like something too important to pause. Even during the World Cup.

1/ The Fable 5 cycle on X is comedy writing itself.
Before the restrictions hit: Timeline was flooded with “I built this entire game/app/SaaS with Fable 5”, wild demos, and “one prompt and it cooked” posts. Everyone was locked in and shipping.
2/ Restrictions drop → instant rage + open source awakening.
“Closed models are a trap.”
“We need sovereign AI now.”
“Time to go local and never rely on these companies again.”
The revolution was trending for like 18 days.
3/ Anthropic announces Fable 5 is back tomorrow… and I think the rage tab will be closed.
The same accounts that were ready to burn closed models to the ground may be back to posting “Fable 5 just built my whole product in 3 prompts” by Wednesday. Demo videos loading. Principles on pause.
4/ This loop is gonna keep repeating until an open source model actually beats Fable 5 (or the next frontier model) and stays better for more than one news cycle.
Until then the “open source or death” movement is just seasonal content that expires the second the shiny toy comes back.
AI Twitter has the memory (and principles) of a goldfish with a trending audio. 😂
Who else is calling it?
#Fable5 #OpenSourceAI

$AMZN $GOOG $MSFT $NVDA

Anthropic re-enabling Claude Fable 5 after disabling it over security / export-control concerns is one of the clearest signals yet:

AI models are crossing from “chatbot” to “autonomous software worker.”

Here’s how insane the game-building capability probably is with one perfect prompt:

Atari / Intellivision era:
full game, no problem

NES / Master System:
full 8-bit platformer, shooter, puzzle game, boss fights, menus, music

SNES / Genesis:
full 16-bit game, RPG systems, beat ‘em up, side-scroller, mode-7 style racer

PS1 / N64 / Saturn:
scoped 3D game, low-poly kart racer, arena fighter, survival horror demo, 3D platformer

PS2 / GameCube / Xbox:
serious indie-scale game or polished vertical slice

PS3 / Xbox 360:
core mechanics + one polished level, not full AAA

PS4 / Xbox One / Switch:
stylized indie game yes, God of War-level production no

PS5 / Series X:
Unreal Engine vertical slice yes, full AAA game no

That’s the real line.

Fable 5 probably can’t one-prompt a full modern AAA game.

But it can likely one-prompt what used to require a small dev team:

game loop
levels
UI
enemy AI
physics
save system
controller support
testing
bug fixing
visual polish

The bottleneck is moving away from code…

and toward assets, taste, QA, optimization, and distribution.

This is why the AI trade is bigger than chat.

The winners are the model layer, cloud layer, compute layer, and agent/tooling layer.

$AMZN Bedrock
$GOOG Cloud
$MSFT AI Foundry
$NVDA inference

We’re not that far from one person prompting a PS2-era quality game into existence over a weekend.

That would have sounded insane/impossible 3 years ago.
